payload.text: [investigation 2026-11-19 basicly session, evidence so far, n=1 per arm] Reading: the load harness, not the claim deadline, makes claims unsettled under CPU load. .scripts/claim_load.py _claim passes --deadline CLAIM_DEADLINE_S / scale (30 / 8 = 3.75 s real), and its git shim scales push and fetch latency by 1/scale, but CPU work (CLI start, folds, share retries) is not scaled, so at scale 8 CPU contention weighs 8 times more against the budget than in real use. Runs on 4 pinned cores (taskset -c 28-31), config sessions=4 machines=2 minutes=8 seed=3: (1) scale 8, quiet: exits {0:6, 3:2}, claim_s mean 6.41 max 8.33 scaled. (2) scale 8, 4 CPU burners on the same cores: exits {0:6, 3:1, 4:1}; the unsettled claim said "the vault refused the share 2 times; 1 events stay queued; run sync again" after claim_s 3.664 s real of 3.75; claim_s mean 18.09 max 29.31 scaled, joined_wait p99 22.6. (3) scale 1, same 4 burners (real 30 s deadline): exits {0:6, 3:2}, claim_s max 3.53 s real. Not yet shown: the failure rate over repeats, and whether a production claim under heavier contention than 4 burners on 4 cores can still exceed 30 s. Test assertion unchanged.

payload.acceptance_criteria:
basicly.toml names the consumers, and for each one its own CI commands. A command basicly consumer-proof builds a wheel from HEAD and, on a fresh clone of each consumer, runs install, a real commit through its hooks and its CI commands. It writes a result tied to the exact commit.
basicly release refuses a cut when no passing result exists for the exact main commit. The refusal names the commit and the command that writes the result.
The release-process skill lists the consumer proof steps.
payload.description:
## Context
When a release is cut, I want a passing consumer proof of that exact main commit, so a consumer defect is caught before publication. 0.46.4, 0.46.5 and 0.46.6 each shipped a consumer defect; the 0.46.6 proof (install plus a real commit) missed terminal's test_basicly_pin_matches_the_installed_harness, which only the consumer's own CI catches. Owner rule: rules ship with enforcement. Orchestrator order 2026-11-19 15:20 UTC, built by the dev session after basicly-qpr2xmr.3.22.

payload.acceptance_criteria:
Hook jobs run without GIT_DIR and GIT_WORK_TREE (pre-push jobs also without GIT_INDEX_FILE). A job that runs git init in another folder leaves the repository config unchanged.
lefthook-runtime refuses by name when core.worktree or core.bare changed during a hook run, and prints the repair command.
A pre-commit check refuses a staged test file whose git subprocess call does not clear the GIT_ variables. It names path:line and the fix, and it keeps a frozen baseline of today's sites.
payload.description:
## Context
When a hook job runs a test that calls git, I want it to run without the snapshot's GIT_ variables, so it can never write the repository's own git config. 2026-11-19 15:24 UTC: terminal's pre-push job ran a test with git init; it inherited GIT_DIR and GIT_WORK_TREE from staged-snapshot and wrote core.worktree = /tmp/basicly-hook-*/tree into terminal's .git/config, and every git call and hook in terminal then failed. Scope: staged-snapshot.py, lefthook-runtime.py, a new check script with its registration, tests, the test-discipline skill line, projections and a changelog fragment. Orchestrator decisions 2026-11-19 15:29 and 15:33 UTC, built by the repair session.
payload.title: Keep hook jobs from writing the repository's git config through inherited GIT_ variables
